problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Minimize Φ(x)=sup_{y∈Y} f(x,y) over E. Nonconvex dependence on x is permitted.

problem_class.label: saddle_point
problem_class.details: Nonconvex–μ-strongly-concave minimax optimization with an unconstrained minimization variable and a nonempty closed convex maximization domain Y. Strong concavity holds on all of F.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: The bundled reply contains ∇f(z), exactly for every history and seed; no oracle error or sampling dependence is present.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Each query at z∈E×F returns the exact value f(z), bundled with its gradient and full Hessian.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Exact full second-order oracle: each bundled call also returns D(∇f)(z) as a continuous linear operator. Queries may lie anywhere in E×F, including outside E×Y.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E and F are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, with the Euclidean product norm on E×F.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Globally L-Lipschitz gradient and ρ-Lipschitz Hessian; 0<μ≤L and ρ>0. Public parameters include Y,L,μ,ρ,Δ,B,ε,x0,y0. Initialization satisfies y0∈Y, Φ(x0)−Φ(x)≤Δ for every x, and ‖∇f(x0,y0)‖≤B, with Δ,B≥0. No boundedness of Y is required.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Return x∈E with ‖∇Φ(x)‖≤ε, where ε>0. Success additionally requires differentiability of Φ on E.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The gradient-norm criterion holds almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, within the supplied fixed oracle budget.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: A standard smooth nonconvex–strongly-concave minimax formulation with convex constraints on the maximization variable, exact second-order information, and value-function first-order stationarity.

descriptionHtml:
Constrained Second-Order Minimax Optimization

We consider minimizing ϕ(x)=supy∈Yf(x,y), where f:E×F→R, E and F are finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, and Y⊆F is nonempty, closed, and convex. The function f has a globally Lipschitz gradient and Hessian and is strongly concave in its second variable. Given initial points have bounded value gap and gradient norm. The oracle returns the value, gradient, and Hessian of f at any queried point. For ε>0, the goal is differentiability of ϕ and an output x¯∈E satisfying ∥∇ϕ(x¯)∥≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Esupy∈Yf(x,y). Equip E×F with the product inner product and norm ∥(x,y)∥=(∥x∥2+∥y∥2)1/2. Write ∇yf(x,y) for the F component of ∇f(x,y). The Hessian ∇2f(z) is the derivative of the gradient, viewed as a linear operator from E×F to itself; ∥⋅∥op denotes its induced operator norm.

The parameters satisfy 0<μ≤L,ρ>0,Δ≥0,B≥0,ε>0. The given initial points are x0∈E and y0∈Y. The algorithm receives E, F, Y, L, μ, ρ, Δ, B, ε, x0, and y0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Second-order regularity). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere, its gradient is Fréchet differentiable everywhere, and, for all z,w∈E×F, ∥∇f(z)−∇f(w)∥≤L∥z−w∥,∥∇2f(z)−∇2f(w)∥op≤ρ∥z−w∥.

Assumption 2 (Strong concavity). For every x∈E and y,y′∈F, f(x,y′)≤f(x,y)+⟨∇yf(x,y),y′−y⟩−μ2∥y′−y∥2.

Assumption 3 (Initial bounds). The initial value gap and full gradient satisfy ϕ(x0)−ϕ(x)≤Δfor every x∈E,∥∇f(x0,y0)∥≤B.

Queries may be made at any z∈E×F, including points whose second component lies outside Y. The exact second-order oracle returns (f(z),∇f(z),∇2f(z)). The output requirement is that ϕ be differentiable everywhere on E and that, after the allotted oracle calls, x¯∈E satisfy ∥∇ϕ(x¯)∥≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
Finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces E,F; nonempty closed convex Y⊆F, possibly unbounded. On all of E×F, ∇f is differentiable and L-Lipschitz, ∇2f is ρ-Lipschitz, and f(x,⋅) is μ-strongly concave. Assume 0<μ≤L, ρ,ε>0, Δ,B≥0, y0∈Y, Φ(x0)−infxΦ(x)≤Δ, and ∥∇f(x0,y0)∥≤B, where Φ(x)=maxy∈Yf(x,y). Exact queries return (f,∇f,∇2f). Target: Φ differentiable and ∥∇Φ(x^)∥≤ε for every seed.

On bounded Y, leading accuracy exponent ε−3/2 instead of ε−2 when r<1; deterministic accuracy. (1) needs full Hessians, ambient Hessian Lipschitzness and B; pays κlog⁡(1+ρB/μ2) startup.

(1): Scope: closed convex dual constraints, including changing active constraints. Matches leading A for Y=F, r≤1, up to logarithms. (1) has κ rather than at most κ startup dependence; for r>1, tracking Ar versus regime-adaptive branches.
(4) ECRN (Zhou et al. 2026, Theorem 11, v1) O~(1+A) gradient/Hessian evaluations; Y=F, ε≤L2/[ρ(4+κ)3/2]; (ε,ρ(4+κ)3/2ε)-SOSP. (1): Scope: closed convex dual constraints. Matches leading A on the unconstrained overlap in the stated accuracy range, up to logarithms. (1) guarantees only first-order stationarity; retains explicit initialization and tracking costs.

D0=Ry+κΔ/L, with Ry=B/μ a valid bound on ∥y0−y∗(x0)∥ when Y=F. O~ suppresses the cited results’ logarithmic factors; SOSP additionally requires ∇2Φ(x^)⪰−ηI for the displayed second tolerance η.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.ProdL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Basic

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.ConstrainedMinimaxSecondOrder

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  F : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [normedF : NormedAddCommGroup F]
  [innerF : InnerProductSpace ℝ F]
  [finiteF : FiniteDimensional ℝ F]
  Y : Set F
  L : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  ρ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  B : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E
  y0 : F

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.finiteE
  Params.normedF Params.innerF Params.finiteF

abbrev Space (p : Params) := WithLp 2 (p.E × p.F)

noncomputable def value {p : Params} (f : Space p → ℝ) (x : p.E) : ℝ :=
  ⨆ y : p.Y, f (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y.1))

structure Regularity (p : Params) (f : Space p → ℝ) : Prop where
  hasGradient : ∀ z, HasGradientAt f (gradient f z) z
  gradient_differentiable : Differentiable ℝ (gradient f)
  gradient_lipschitz : ∀ z w, ‖gradient f z - gradient f w‖ ≤ p.L * ‖z - w‖
  hessian_lipschitz : ∀ z w,
    ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient f) z - fderiv ℝ (gradient f) w‖ ≤ p.ρ * ‖z - w‖
  strongly_concave : ∀ x y y',
    f (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y')) ≤ f (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y)) +
      ⟪(gradient f (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y))).snd, y' - y⟫ - p.μ / 2 * ‖y' - y‖ ^ 2

structure Assumptions (p : Params) (f : Space p → ℝ) : Prop extends Regularity p f where
  initial_gap : ∀ x, value f p.x0 - value f x ≤ p.Δ
  initial_gradient : ‖gradient f (WithLp.toLp 2 (p.x0, p.y0))‖ ≤ p.B

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Space p → ℝ
  Query p := Space p
  Reply p := ℝ × Space p × (Space p →L[ℝ] Space p)
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := id
  valid p := 0 < p.μ ∧ p.μ ≤ p.L ∧ 0 < p.ρ ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ p.B ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧
    IsClosed p.Y ∧ Convex ℝ p.Y ∧ p.y0 ∈ p.Y
  admissible p f oracle :=
    Assumptions p f ∧
    (∀ k seed z, oracle.answer k (0, z) seed =
      (f z, gradient f z, fderiv ℝ (gradient f) z))
  successful p f output law :=
    Differentiable ℝ (value f) ∧
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(law : MeasureTheory.Measure _), ‖gradient (value f) (output ω)‖ ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.ConstrainedMinimaxSecondOrder
